test_title: SSC MTS Previous Year Paper (Held on: 12 July 2022 Shift 2)
subject: general
question: On a certain sum of money, the simple interest for 2 years is ₹150 at the rate of 10% per annum. What is the difference between the compound interest and the simple interest for 2 years if, in the case of compound interest, interest is compounded annually at the rate of 10% per annum.
solution: **Given:** Simple interest for 2 years = ₹150 Rate of interest = 10% per annum **Concept Used:** Simple Interest = (P x R x T)/100 where, P is the principal amount, R is the rate of interest, and T is the time period. Compound Interest = P x (1 + R/100)T - P where, P is the principal amount, R is the rate of interest, and T is the time period.
